correctness.rationale: The frozen Finding overstates the classification by saying 'exact marker separation'. At n=10,s=3, the zero-based pairs (2,7) and (3,6) have separations 5 and 3 but both yield (G00,G01,G10,G11)=(19,4,4,1) and identical singleton counts. The complete corrected RESULT.md in repairs/2 replaces that assertion with the observed long/short indicator and explicitly exhibits the collision; the formulas, scope and threshold are unchanged. The corrected proof was re-audited: fixing length and weight makes (e,G01,G10) equivalent to the whole observation. With r=s-1,H=n-2s+1 the boundary layer j is G01+G10+2e-2H and the remaining coordinate is G01. Short central gaps 1 and 2 fill the parity ranges when r>=2; for r=1 only adjacent pairs occur. Positive-excess short pairs cannot cross the two boundaries for H>=r. For 1<=j<=r the left range is [0,r-j] and the reflected range starts at 2H-r+2j. For r<j<2r each side has one value and j=2r is impossible. Central long pairs reduce to sums of two integers 0<=x<=y'<=H-r-1 (all intermediate sums occur). For j=1,...,r the long-pair left/central, opposite-boundary and central/right runs have consecutive G01 ranges [r-j,H-1], [H,H+j-2], [H+j-1,2H+2j-r-2], with the middle empty for j=1. For j>r, only opposite boundaries work and their split gives 2r-j+1 values. The sums give both asserted linear branches. When H=r all counts just listed remain valid except central long pairs, now absent rather than the formal linear count -1; this proves the exact +1 correction. One representative per deck is a maximum distinguishable code. Independently ran `python3 /workspace/review_checks.py 2`: 35 parameter cases from s=2 through 8 and n=3s-2 through 3s+2, using literal position-pair enumeration, plus the exact separation collision. Neither this finite reproduction nor static inspection of the frozen checker substitutes for the interval argument.

value.rationale: The exact image size measures a natural noiseless sparse reconstruction limit: quadratically many inputs collapse to linearly many distinguishable ones.
